posts.cooked:
Unity, Void Guard Writhe, And Prime Wardens Tempest must recapture that merc-with-a-pain-in-the-derriere-cloaking-device Ambuscade, who has escaped his cell and is running wild in The Block! Hijinks ensue!

Easy mint, with the outcome never really in doubt. Ambuscade never got most of his damaging devices in play, other than a couple of Sonic Mines, easily neutralized in the first instance by Writhe’s Lies Of The Shadows by turning its own damage debuff against it, and in the second, by the Block Guard responsible for its destruction in the first place. His Reactive Plating could do little more than plink at Unity’s Stealth Bot, while the heroes hit him with everything but the kitchen sink!

The environment turned out to be pretty benign in this game - Tempest was able to play Flash Flood to remove nasty cards like Char (ugh!), and Defensive Displacement hampered Ansel while the heroes inflicted irreducible damage courtesy of Writhe’s Nowhere To Hide.

A Hasty Augmentation to give Writhe a big boost on his Concealed Assailant, a few rounds of Platform Bot damage, and Gene Bound Shackles coming out early to let Tempest really bring the thunder spelled quick incapacitation, and hopefully more secure accommodations, for Ambuscade!

Screenshot_20210907-1027351080×2460 170 KB

posts.cooked: This showed up at like 1 in the morning for me, and I considered doing it immediately (as I did last week when Plague Rat attacked Megalopolis at a similarly early hour), but Ambuscade is a villain I’m somewhat less familiar with, and I didn’t want to risk losing a Mint due to rewinding because I forgot how a card worked. So as of this posting I still haven’t played this one; instead, I’ve been replaying all the old weeklies with Ambuscade in them, trying to get very practiced in dealing with him. Interestingly, his second ever appearance in the Weeklies was in this same environment, and also featured a three-hero team with Unity in position 1.

Went ahead and beat it, easily and without even being significantly tempted to Undo. Unlike several other posters, I didn’t use Lies of the Shadows (a card I find annoying, because it prompts you constantly throughout the round; I don’t know of any other way it could work, so I just avoid using it in general). I don’t recall exactly what I did do (aside from dropping Otherworldly Resilience so that Tempest could use Arc of Power totally unrestrained during the Defensive Displacement turn, dealing irreducible damage to Ambuscade because of Writhe), but it was nothing particularly out of the ordinary. An awful game for Unity because she had so few Bots, but still an easy win against a villain who I’ve only EVER lost against on Challenge mode.

posts.cooked:
starkenburg_alexander:

FYI, if you click/press and hold on the “Do you want to destroy the Shadow Cloak” prompt (or any prompt, like Twist the Ether), you can set it to Yes/No/Whatever for either that turn or the entire game.

This I knew.

If you want to cancel a choice you made, you can hit the lightning bolt at the top of the screen to see active effects and clear the choice.

This I didn’t. Thanks!

The big issue with Lies of the Shadows is that it asks you a question for every single instance of damage, and because you can only destroy the Shadow Cloak once, the answer will default to “no” most of the time, but could shift to “yes” any moment when a big hit shows up. I can’t think of any reasonably easy solution to this issue; I’ll just have to wait until our AI technology gets good enough that the interface of SOTMTVG is no longer limited to buttons. Then I can tell the AI something like “say No to all Lies of the Shadows triggers unless they deal at least 4 damage, except those with a cannot-deal-damage rider attached or the like”. Until then, it’ll just be a card that I rarely want to use, like Haka’s Punish the Weak or Tempest’s Violent Cyclone. Doesn’t mean I don’t like those heroes, and Writhe is probably still in my top ten, despite one or two cards I tend to avoid.
